title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint found administratively out of order under OMSJC 9.1.a. and dismissed as prematurely filed; the SJC held it could not be put in order because BCO 43-2 did not require South Florida Presbytery to consider the complaint before its next stated meeting. The approved officers' recommendation also stated that the petitioner's BCO 40-5 application was prematurely filed with the SJC. No merits determination was made.
first_summary: A complaint filed with the SJC before South Florida Presbytery had considered it was found administratively out of order and dismissed as premature. The SJC relied on BCO 43-2, which does not require a court to consider a complaint until its next stated meeting, and concluded the case could not be put in order. No merits were reached.
summary: The SJC dismissed John B. Thompson's complaint against South Florida Presbytery as administratively out of order and prematurely filed. Because BCO 43-2 did not require the presbytery to consider the complaint until its next stated meeting, and that meeting had not yet occurred, the SJC held the case could not be put in order under the BCO or OMSJC. The unanimous officers' recommendation also called Thompson's BCO 40-5 application premature. No merits were reached.
